impl.summary:
I fixed all three findings on branch fix/review-wait in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-review-wait (commit 8cd355f). All three were still present in the code at 2834604. The targeted tests pass (46 tests). The new tests fail on the old code for the intended reasons.

**Finding 0 (P1), a finished lane's deadline ended the question pause.** In `wait_handoffs` (workflow/automatic.py), each lane is now located and its completion file read before the deadline check. A completion accepted while the session is idle or done skips the check, because the deadline runs from launch to the completion signal. A question still meets the deadline check before it is recorded, as before. In the WorkerQuestion test I removed the line that gave the finished lane a new launch time; with the real launch time, the old code raised "Worker adapter deadline exhausted". I also added `test_a_finished_lane_is_not_held_to_its_deadline_while_another_lane_waits_on_a_question`. It replays the review's scenario: adapter finishes at t=100, ui asks at T-600 and is still waiting at T+1, is answered at T+60 and completes at T+650. The wait returns with no raise and no stop, and `paused_seconds` is 660.

**Finding 2, a session working again was recorded as an operator answer.** There are two fixes in workflow/guardrails.py:
- **Recording the placeholder:** the new `record_pane_answer` checks and writes under one `question_lock`. It does nothing if `answer` recorded an answer in the meantime, so the ValueError that made drive() stop every worker is gone.
- **Letting `answer` still work:** `record_answer` may now replace the controller's placeholder (`PANE_ANSWER`, reworded to "(no answer recorded: the worker's session worked again in its pane)") and deliver the text. The deadline keeps running.

The controller's event now says the session is working again and that `answer` can still record and deliver an answer. The test covers:
- the session working again with nobody answering, after which `answer` succeeds and delivers;
- a lane going working, idle, working with no question waiting, which is not recorded as an answer;
- a lane that never asked, which gets no questions file;
- an `answer` landing between the controller's check and its write, simulated by patching `waiting_question`. On the old loop this raised ValueError; on the new one it does not.

**Finding 13, a question was read only when the native state was idle or done.** The job timelines in ~/.claude/jobs show the real native states: finished turns report `done`, and turns that end waiting on the user report `blocked` (for example "awaiting user to test locally" and "2 design choices need your call"). The registry accepts idle, working, blocked and done. A question completion is now recorded in idle, done or blocked. A lane that is blocked on a recorded question no longer gets the second "needs attention" event. The new test `test_a_question_is_recorded_in_every_state_a_turn_ends_in` runs once per state (idle, done, blocked) and checks `ui.questions.json`, `ui.deadline.json`, a delivered `answer`, the handoff and the exact events. Before the fix the blocked case failed.

The fix/autoupdate rule is unchanged: a TransientInfraError from the session listing still leaves the wait before any of this and stops nothing.

I updated workflow/README.md and workflow/RUNBOOK.md in their existing voice: the "Worker questions" paragraph and the `answer` paragraph, the placeholder text and the advice not to run `answer` after typing the answer in the pane, and the test-coverage line.

decisions: A `completed` or `blocked` completion file is still accepted only when the native state is idle or done, as in slice 1 and its existing test test_blocked_worker_waits_for_attention_instead_of_ending_the_run. Only a question is read in the blocked state. The verifier called accepting completed files under blocked a separate decision, and the `blocked` state can also mean a prompt in the middle of a turn. I kept the smaller change.

When the session is blocked and a completion file exists, the file is now validated (read_signal). A malformed, stale or foreign file then blocks the run as it does in idle or done, where before it waited until the deadline. The turn is over, so the file is final.

The deadline check still runs before a question is recorded. A question first seen after its lane's deadline (for example after a controller restart) raises as before, instead of pausing a deadline that has already run out.

For finding 2 I did not use the reviewer's first suggestion (leave `answer` null after the session resumes). The projects contract allows only the latest question to wait and requires an answer to come with its time, so a later question would make the export invalid. Instead the controller records a placeholder that claims no answer, and `workflow answer` may replace it.

I changed the placeholder text from "(answered by typing in the worker's pane)" to "(no answer recorded: the worker's session worked again in its pane)", because the session may have woken on its own. Entries recorded by older runs with the old text cannot be replaced by `answer`, which is the old behaviour.
When `answer` replaces the placeholder, the deadline is not extended again. It has been running since the session worked again, and the time between is not known to be waiting.

I did not persist a `completed_at`. The completion is re-read on every poll, so a lane that becomes `working` again after writing its file is held to its deadline again, and a completion signal still requires the turn to have ended.

To avoid merge conflicts with fix/bg-settings, I kept RUNBOOK edits to the Worker questions and `answer` paragraphs and the test-coverage line. I did not edit the automatic-mode paragraph (line 34), which holds the exit-75 wording.
not_done: I did not run the full suite (workflow.run_tests) or Playwright; per the assignment the integrator runs them after the merge.

wait_reviews (the native reviewer wait in automatic.py) also reads a completion only when the session is idle or done. A reviewer whose final turn reports `blocked` still waits until its deadline. This was outside this assignment and is not changed.
docs/PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW.md 4.6 does not describe the placeholder answer or the `blocked` state for questions. Only the README and RUNBOOK were updated.

Separate from this change: if the controller never sees a session in the `working` state (for example it was down while the worker ran after an answer typed in the pane), a completed lane can still keep an unanswered question in the record. This was not in the findings and is not changed.

problems.description: record_answer now replaces PANE_ANSWER unconditionally, so `answer` is accepted for as long as the lane's latest question has the placeholder. That includes after the lane's completion was accepted, the handoff was saved and freeze stopped the worker. Before this branch the same command was refused ('Worker ui has no unanswered question'). deliver_answer then types the text and Enter into the lane's Herdr pane. Once the controller has stopped the worker, attach-one returns and the pane is an idle shell in the tool's source checkout, so the answer text runs as a shell command. The controller's own event invites this ('`answer` still records and delivers an answer'). The RUNBOOK only warns against it; no guard enforces it.
problems.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with the WorkerQuestion fixture (scratch probe_answer.py). ui asks a question and the operator types the answer in the pane. The controller records PANE_ANSWER, ui completes (done), wait_handoffs returns and ui.handoff.json exists. I then added ui.stop.json. `workflow answer RUN ui "Use option B"` exits 0, records the answer and makes the Herdr calls [send-text pane-ui 'Use option B'], [send-keys pane-ui Enter]. On 2834604 the same sequence exits 1: 'Blocked: Worker ui has no unanswered question'.
problems.fix: Only replace PANE_ANSWER while the lane is still on that question. In record_answer, still under question_lock, refuse to replace the placeholder when `<node>.stop.json`, `<node>.handoff.json` or a new `<node>.completion.json` exists, keeping the old 'has no unanswered question' refusal. Add a WorkerQuestion case: a pane-answered question, the lane completes, and `answer` is refused with no Herdr call.

problems.description: The controller treats a waiting question as answered in the pane only when a poll sees the native state `working`. The native job timelines the branch cites show that this state change may never be observed. In ~/.claude/jobs/4bf1998b/timeline.jsonl, the user's reply to a `blocked` session is logged as `blocked` (19:42:09, detail = the typed text). The reply turn then runs 2.5 minutes with no `working` entry and ends `done` at 19:44:52. A reply to a `done` session also stays `done` for 17 s (19:46:04 to 19:46:21). This branch now records questions under `blocked`, which makes that path reachable for the documented 'type the answer in the pane' flow. When `working` is never observed, the question stays waiting, the lane's deadline stays paused for the whole reply turn (an unbounded worker), and the next signal is recorded on top of a still-waiting question.
problems.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with the WorkerQuestion fixture (scratch probe_blocked.py). ui is `blocked` and asks Q1, which is recorded and paused. The operator types in the pane and the state stays `blocked`. ui then ends on a second question. Result: ui.questions.json holds [(1, None), (2, None)] and ui.deadline.json keeps paused_at from Q1, so no deadline ran during the reply turn. Two waiting questions break the run-inputs contract ('Only the latest question of ui can be waiting', contracts/projects/v1.ts:389), so the served inputs are refused. If ui instead ends `done` with a completed file, the handoff is accepted while Q1 still shows as waiting. The viewer then says the deadline is paused, and `answer` stays accepted after the finish.
problems.fix: Treat any new completion signal read while the lane's latest question still waits as proof that the session worked again. Before record_question or accepting the handoff, call record_pane_answer(runtime.directory, node, clock) when waiting_question(...) is truthy (it is already a locked no-op once `answer` landed). Emit the same 'working again' event. Test that a Q1 recorded under `blocked` followed by Q2 (and separately by a completed file) with no `working` poll leaves Q1 with the placeholder, only the latest question waiting and the deadline resumed. Qualify the README/RUNBOOK sentence 'records ... as soon as the session works again' accordingly.

problems.description: 'a lane that finished early never ends the run while another lane waits on its answer' overclaims. A finished lane is exempt only while its session reports idle or done. If its session reports `blocked` (the slice-1 rule does not accept a completed file under blocked) or works again after its original deadline, the lane is held to its launch + worker_timeout deadline again, and drive() stops every worker. Real native timelines show finished turns classified `blocked` ('UI worker ready; awaiting task input' in 4370b992, 'review complete; awaiting Write grant' in dccd22b5). The branch's own comment says a file under `blocked` is final.
problems.failure_scenario: adapter writes a valid completed file and its turn ends classified `blocked`. ui waits on a question past adapter's original deadline. wait_handoffs raises 'Worker adapter deadline exhausted' and drive() stops ui.
problems.fix: Either accept a valid `completed` file under `blocked` too (the file is final once the turn is over, which is the same reasoning used for questions), or keep slice 1's rule and reword the RUNBOOK. In that case say the exemption holds only while the finished session reports idle or done, and record the blocked-finished case as an open decision.

problems.description: When `answer` later replaces PANE_ANSWER, the controller emits no event: (node, n) is already in `answered`. The timeline shows only 'working again while question n waits', never the operator's real answer. Separately, in the new finished-lane test, `self.runtime.stop_workers = lambda: self.fail(...)` asserts nothing, because wait_handoffs never calls stop_workers (drive() does).
problems.failure_scenario: In test_a_session_working_again_without_an_answer..., the operator's 'Use option B' at t=50 produces no event (len(self.events) == 2). In the finished-lane test, the no-stop assertion would pass even if drive() stopped the workers.
problems.fix: Track answered entries by (node, n, answer) so that a replaced placeholder emits 'question n answered', or have answer_main append an event. Drop the vacuous stop_workers stub, or state that no raise is what guarantees drive() stops nothing.

fix.summary:
Both P2 problems were real, and both are fixed in commit a035f73 on fix/review-wait (worktree /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-review-wait).

(1) The `answer` command could type into a stopped worker's shell. record_answer now checks a new helper, went_on, in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-review-wait/workflow/guardrails.py. The check runs under question_lock, before anything is recorded. `answer` is refused (still "has no unanswered question", now with the reason) once the worker has moved past its latest question. Three things show that: a new `<lane>.completion.json`, since record_question moves the question's own file away; `<lane>.handoff.json`; or `<lane>.stop.json`. The refusal covers the pane placeholder and a still-null answer. undelivered_answer gets the same guard, so rerunning a failed delivery cannot type into the pane either.

(2) wait_handoffs in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-review-wait/workflow/automatic.py used to record a pane-typed reply only when a poll saw `working`. Now a completion signal read while the latest question waits also counts as proof. It records the placeholder via record_pane_answer and resumes the deadline before that signal is recorded as a question or accepted as a handoff. So at most one question waits, and a handoff never leaves a question open. The answer events are now emitted before a lane's handoff is collected, so a lane that finishes in the same poll no longer loses them. The event for the signal case says `answer` is refused for that question. The event for the `working` case says `answer` still works until the worker's next completion signal.

The fixes from the earlier commit are unchanged: P1 (a finished lane is not held to its deadline), finding 2 and finding 13 (a question is recorded in idle, done or blocked). A TransientInfraError from the inventory still leaves the loop first and stops nothing, and CompletionTests and ClaudeUnavailableTests pass. README and RUNBOOK now describe the refusal and when the controller notices a reply typed in the pane.

Tests were written first, and each failed before its fix:
- WorkerQuestion.test_a_completion_signal_written_while_a_question_waits_shows_the_session_worked_again: question 1 recorded while the session is blocked or done, then question 2 or a completed file with no `working` poll, in all four combinations. It checks that question 1 gets the placeholder, only the latest question waits, the deadline accounting, the events, and that an `answer` before the controller reads the signal is refused.
- WorkerQuestion.test_answer_types_nothing_once_the_worker_went_on_from_its_question: a question answered in the pane; `answer` is refused with no Herdr call after the new completion file, after the handoff, and after the stop.
- AnswerDelivery.test_a_rerun_types_nothing_once_the_worker_went_on: rerunning a failed delivery is refused, with and without --no-herdr.

decisions: The went_on guard applies whenever `answer` would record, whether the latest answer is null or the placeholder, not only when replacing the placeholder. A new completion file while a question waits means the worker has moved on: it wrote a new question or finished. A null-answer `answer` would then be typed as a reply to the wrong turn, for example while the controller is down between polls. So refusing is the safer choice.

The same guard was added to undelivered_answer (rerunning a failed delivery). It is the same hazard through the same command: after the operator typed the answer in the pane and freeze stopped the worker, a rerun would type into the shell. It never blocks a legitimate rerun, because while the worker still waits on the question its completion file has been moved away and there is no handoff or stop.

went_on checks stop.json, handoff.json and completion.json for that lane, as the reviewer proposed. In a real run a stale handoff cannot sit beside a new question: the wait saves every lane's handoff at once, then freeze stops the workers. workflow repair on fix/lane-repair forks checkpoints after the handoff and relaunches no worker session. The WorkerQuestion fixture, which reuses ui after a wait saved its handoff, now drops that handoff in its ask() helper, with a comment.

The deadline is still paused during a reply turn that the registry never reports as `working`. It resumes when the next completion signal is read, which is the reviewer's proposed fix. `claude agents` rows show no finer activity signal that the controller reads, and the RUNBOOK now says so; running `answer` restarts the deadline immediately.

Two event texts instead of one reused event. When a poll saw `working`, the event says `answer` still records and delivers until the worker's next completion signal. When a new completion signal proved the reply, the event says `answer` is refused for that question. A single text would have told the operator that `answer` still works when it is refused.

problems.description: The P1 fix only exempts a finished lane from its deadline while its session is idle or done. The exemption is re-decided on every poll and never persisted. When a finished lane's session changes to `working` or `blocked` again (the operator types into its Herdr pane, or a background command it started ends and wakes it), `item` is None (working) or the `row["state"] != "blocked"` guard fails (blocked). The lane then drops back into the deadline check with its original launch + worker_timeout_seconds. So this is still the finding-0 failure: a question pause in another lane lasts only until a finished lane shows any activity after its original deadline. At that point drive() stops every worker, including the one working on the operator's answer, and blocks the run. This contradicts the definition the fix cites (CLI help: 'per-worker deadline from launch to completion signal'; this lane's valid completed file is still there). impl.summary: I implemented version 1 of lane repair on fix/lane-repair (worktree /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-lane-repair) in one commit. The new workflow/repair.py adds `python -m workflow repair "$RUN" <lane>[,<lane>] --commit <sha> --reason ... [--dry-run]` and `--workspace`. It keeps a repairs.json journal with idempotent steps S0-S6 (a crashed repair completes when the identical command is rerun). It builds one snapshot commit per lane that comes out the same on a rerun (parent = base, private index, fixed dates, refs under refs/workflow-repair/<h16>/<n>/), reusing freeze's ownership rules (moved into Pipeline.check_ownership) plus the symlink, gitlink and no-op checks. It forks from the newest checkpoint whose next step is exactly the verify fan-out, passing that checkpoint's own config and id, and checks the state after the fork. It refuses with exit 1 and 'Blocked:' in every case the design lists. It never launches a session, runs a check or invokes the graph, and prints `automatic --live` or `retry` as the way to continue. pipeline.py: the attempt limit counts from each repair's floor in attempt/retry_check; candidate generations candidate-<g>.json and candidate-<g>/; candidate() refuses worker packets whose commit differs from the lane snapshot and a candidate whose tree differs from the repair's expected tree; retry refuses while a repair is recorded; status lists repairs and repair_workspaces; the report has a Repairs section. automatic.py: the identical-failure guard compares only attempts of the same revision and uses the floor; drive appends a 'controller blocked' event when the guard or the attempt limit stops it; drive refuses while a repair is recorded; the reviewer prompt gets one line per repair naming repair-<n>.diff. Docs: a RUNBOOK section 'Blocked after freeze: repair a lane' walks through 001's case; attempts now read 'per lane, phase and revision'; new command and file rows; README command row and module list. The 13 new tests in workflow/test_repair.py cover the design's cases with real git repos, checkpoints and checks and no Playwright; they failed before implementation and pass now (about 28 s). I also confirmed each pipeline and automatic change fails its test when reverted. The existing non-Playwright tests I ran on the touched code pass. I did not run the Playwright-backed classes in test_automatic and test_pipeline that also exercise the changed candidate() and drive().

review.notes:
Verdict: problems, because of one P1. A second repair is impossible once the first repair's continuation fails in the worker phase.

Why: a failed verify superstep does not create a new checkpoint, so the head stays the fork (`head_after`). blocked_run then treats the run as "not continued". It refuses both `--commit` and `--workspace`, and points the operator to `automatic --live`, which fails identically again. Two ordinary cases hit this: an incomplete first fix, and a worker-phase block of two lanes, which needs one repair per lane. The fix is one condition: refuse only when the head is the fork and no task has an error. My probe shows the rest of the flow (fork point, targets, fork, continuation) then works.

What holds up against the real 001 data and the code:
- **The 001 case works on a copy of the real run.** The fork is taken from 1f1b78a9 with `fork.config`, and `update_state` is never called on the head.
- **Candidate generation paths.** `candidate()` is the only reader of `candidate.json`; reviewers use the bundle's candidate commit.
- **Coherence assertions and attempts.** Both new `candidate()` assertions are in place. Floors in `attempt`, `retry_check` and `advance_failed_checks` behave exactly as before at floor 1, so old run directories are unaffected. The same-revision guard is in place.
- **Refusals while a repair is `recorded`.** `drive()` (so `automatic` and `automatic-step`) and `retry` refuse.
- **Crash recovery.** A crash after each of S1 to S5 is completed by rerunning the identical command: the snapshot commits are deterministic (commit-tree with pinned dates) and exactly one fork is written.
- **Launches and the source checkout.** No `claude` process is started (the subprocess test checks this). The source checkout's working tree and index are never written.
- **Outputs.** `status`, `report` and the review prompt change only when `repairs.json` exists.
- **Docs.** README and RUNBOOK are accurate.

Deviations from the design that I think are correct:
- The source ref is `.../<n>/source_commit` rather than `.../<n>/source`. Lane ids cannot contain `_`, so it cannot collide with a lane, whereas `source` is a legal lane id.
- The private index lives in a temp directory rather than `$RUN/repair-<n>-<lane>.index`.

Merge risk: automatic.py `drive()` gains two lines (the `refuse_recorded` import and call) and `advance_or_block` at the error-classification line. fix/review-wait also works in `automatic.py`, so check that hunk when merging.

fix.summary:
The reviewer's P1 was real, and it is fixed on fix/lane-repair in the worktree /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-lane-repair.

The bug: `blocked_run` refused a second repair, and the `--workspace` helper, whenever the head checkpoint was the last repair's `head_after`. It read that as "the run has not continued from it". But a failed verify superstep writes no new checkpoint. LangGraph stores the error as a pending write on the same checkpoint. So when the continuation after repair 1 failed the repaired lane's own check again, the head was still the fork, and the run could not be recovered. I reproduced this with the reviewer's probe (scratchpad/probe_worker_refail.py): repair 2 exited 1 with "Repair 1 is applied and the run has not continued from it". At that point the head was `head_after`, `next` was ('verify_adapter',) and verify_adapter had an error pending.

The fix is in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-lane-repair/workflow/repair.py, `blocked_run`. The refusal now fires only when the head is the last fork AND no task has an error:
`if applied and state.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"] == applied[-1]["head_after"] and not any(task.error for task in state.tasks):`
The fork still passes `fork.config`, which carries its checkpoint_id. The pending error and the other lanes' pending writes therefore stay on the failed branch, as they do for the first repair. `fork_point` still finds this checkpoint: `get_state_history` does not apply pending writes, so its `next` is still the verify fan-out. Crash recovery is unchanged, because `head_before` equals `fork_from` and `fork_run`'s idempotence checks still hold.

New test: class `RepairAfterWorkerRefailure` in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-lane-repair/workflow/test_repair.py. It is independent and uses the existing fakes and real temporary git repos. The steps:
1. The adapter unit check fails twice identically.
2. Repair 1 applies an incomplete fix (VALUE = 3).
3. A second `--commit` and `--workspace` are both refused, with "has not continued" and nothing written. This covers the refusal that stays.
4. `drive()` fails the repaired lane at attempts 3 and 4, and the head is still `head_after`.
5. `--workspace` is detached at repair 1's snapshot. Repair 2 (VALUE = 2) forks from `head_after` with targets {worker:adapter: 5}, and the head after the fork has `next == verify fan-out` with no errors.
6. `drive()` then passes worker/adapter/5 and builds candidate-2. The reviewer prompt names repair 2, and the fix is integrated.

This test failed before the fix at the `--workspace` step, with the reported error, and passes after it.

In /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-lane-repair/workflow/RUNBOOK.md, the sentence "An applied repair is not replaced" now says the refusal holds only before the run continues from the repair. Once the continuation stops at a check verdict again, including the repaired lane's own check, the next repair builds on it.

Any task error on `head_after` must come from a continuation, because `fork_run` asserts the fork has no errors when it creates it. A continuation that was interrupted without an error is still refused with 'continue with automatic --live', which is the right advice.

No change to fork_point, fork_run or crash recovery. `get_state_history` does not apply pending writes (checked in langgraph 1.2.11 `_prepare_state_snapshot`), so the fork checkpoint still has `next == fan-out` and repair 1's snapshots. `update_state(fork.config)` with a checkpoint_id does not carry the pending writes, so a lane whose verify succeeded on the failed branch is rechecked from its existing packet.

recheck.notes:
Verdict: ok. The round-1 P1 is fixed, and I found no new P0, P1 or P2 problems.

**The P1 fix (6e1c13c).** blocked_run now refuses only when the head is the last repair's fork and no task on it has an error. The fix works for these reasons:
- A failed verify superstep leaves the fork as the head with the error pending.
- A repair from that head passes fork.config, which carries the checkpoint_id. In langgraph 1.2.11, bulk_update_state then does not apply the pending writes: I read the source to confirm. The new test also asserts that next is the verify fan-out and that there are no errors after repair 2.
- Before any continuation, both `--commit` and `--workspace` are still refused and nothing is written. The test covers this.
- A continuation interrupted with no error still gets "continue with automatic --live", which is the right advice.
- The recorded path (crash recovery) never calls blocked_run, so it is unchanged.

Both dead ends named in round 1 now reach integration:
- a first fix that fails the lane's own check again (the new test);
- two lanes blocked at the worker phase, repaired one per repair (my probe).

The RUNBOOK sentence and the code comment are accurate.

**Other checks:**
- With no repairs.json, the attempt bounds are unchanged from before (floor 1).
- Old runs still use candidate.json and candidate/.
- repair launches nothing: the CLI test's fake `claude` is never called and the fake launch log is unchanged.
- drive() and retry refuse while a repair is recorded.
- The guard's new `controller blocked` event and its longer message do not break existing tests: test_automatic matches only "failed identically on attempts 1 and 2".
- The `status` additions are additive keys.
- No schema limits the attempt number.
- The worktree is clean at 6e1c13c, and the live run directory has no repair files.
